newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hungarian minister confident of NATO entry.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian minister confident of NATO entry.

text.p: Hungary said on Monday it was confident it would be in the first wave of former communist countries invited to join NATO after the alliance's summit meeting in Madrid in July.
"We have confidence we will be invited for membership negotiations (to NATO)," Hungarian Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti told a news briefing after meeting Dutch Defence Minister Joris Voorhoeve.
He said Hungary had progressed sufficiently in military, political and security matters to be able to sit back calmly and await the Madrid summit's decision.
Asked if Hungary would back NATO membership for Romania and Slovenia, Keleti said it was in Hungary's interest for as many central European countries as possible to join the alliance.

But he said NATO should screen applicants closely according to criteria such as an irreversible transition to democracy, the establishment of a market economy, a policy towards minority peoples in line with generally accepted European norms and 'good neighbourliness'.
"Neither Romania nor Slovenia are competitors of ours (in seeking to join NATO) but this is not a hand-in-hand process," he said.

Voorhoeve said the Netherlands and Hungary had similar views on restoring public order in Albania, but said he could not be more specific ahead of a report by a European Union assessment mission to the region.
"It is difficult to say right now what prospects there are for establishing control...and where the international community could be of assistance," he said.
But he said it was clear that joint action was required. "If anarchy prevails and economic stagnation continues (Albania) will remain a trouble spot and the source of many refugees," he said.

Keleti's visit was aimed at improving military ties between Hungary and the Netherlands, which already cooperate on 39 training, technology and military intelligence projects. They signed a Memorandum of Understanding to step up bilateral defence links.
